input.question: How is it possible that everything falls at the same speed regardless of mass? Is there a limit where this approximation stops to be correct?
input.ground_truth: > Is there a limit where this approximation stops to be correct? Yes. The "limit of the approximation" is that the mass of the thing dropped is negligible compared to the mass of the Earth. Consider two masses M1 and M2 at a distance R. The gravitational force F between them will be G\*M1\*M2/R^2 , so the acceleration of the first object will be F/M1 = G\*M2/R^2 and the acceleration of the second object will be F/M2 = G\*M1/R^2 The two objects will thus accelerate towards each other at a rate of G\*(M1 + M2)/R^2 . In the case of a feather or hammer on the Earth, M1 is so much larger than M2 that the effects of M2 can be ignored. In this case, both hammer and feather would have the same acceleration.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How is it possible that everything falls at the same speed regardless of mass? Is there a limit where this approximation stops to be correct?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you have a feather and a rock. If you drop them at the same time on Earth, they both hit the ground at the same time (if there’s no air, like on the Moon). This happens because the Earth pulls everything equally hard, but heavier things are harder to move. It’s like trying to push a toy car and a big truck—the car is easy to move, but the truck is heavy. But the pull is strong enough to make up for that!

So, the Earth pulls harder on the heavy thing, but it’s also harder to move. That’s why they fall at the same speed.

But… if you drop them where there’s air, like here on Earth, the feather falls slower because the air pushes against it. So the “same speed” rule only works if there’s no air, or if you don’t care about the air.

Also, if things are really, really heavy or really, really fast, or if we’re not on Earth but somewhere with a different gravity, this rule changes a little. But for most things we drop every day, they fall at the same speed!
